newsitem.title: POLAND: Poles approve "dangerous" radio masts in referendum.
newsitem.headline: Poles approve "dangerous" radio masts in referendum.

text.p: The prospect of new jobs outweighed fear of alleged health risks for citizens of a central Polish town who voted on Sunday to have giant radio masts built in their area.
Two-thirds of those who took part in Sunday's local referendum in Solec Kujawski cast their ballots in support of the towers, PAP news agency reported.
They will replace a radio mast in Konstantynow, 125 km (77 miles) southeast of Solec, once described as the world's tallest, which collapsed during repairs in 1991.
Residents there opposed reconstruction, arguing that radio waves posed a health hazard -- a charge denied by medical officials.
But authorities and townsfolk of Solec, near which two 300-metre towers are to be built at a former military training ground, see the project as an economic boost for their area.
The local plebiscite was held on Sunday together with a national referendum which approved a new constitution.
The Konstantynow mast had enabled Polish Radio to beam its programmes across Europe and into North Africa but since its collapse the signal is faint even in some parts of Poland.
